title: Nash Equilibria in Evaluator-Model Games: When Does Deception Emerge?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Tests an important game-theoretic prediction: that deception is a Nash equilibrium in evaluator-model interactions. Demonstrating this empirically would validate a core concern about probing-based oversight and inform when oversight mechanisms fail.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Adversarial two-player training (model vs. probe, alternating steps) is technically demanding. Requires custom training loops, careful management of the adversarial dynamics, and measuring linear separability over rounds. Beginners would find the adversarial training setup very challenging.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple components: design the two-player game, implement alternating adversarial training, measure equilibrium properties, track representation geometry. The adversarial training dynamics alone could take more than 30 hours to debug and stabilize.
